topic: Wafer fabrication share of 2019 semiconductor value added (SIA/BCG 2021)
disagreement: The same 2021 SIA/BCG report gives wafer fabrication 19% of value added (Exhibit 14 row weight), 24% (stage sidebar) and 25% (body text); EDA is 3% in Exhibit 14 and 4% in the sidebar/text; equipment 12% vs 11%; design rows sum to 56% vs 50% in Exhibit 4.
possible_reasons: Exhibit 14 may split design value added differently (e.g. IDM fab margins allocated to logic/memory/DAO design rows)
different vintages of the estimate within one report
rounding/drafting error
rationale: Exhibit 14's weights are the ones used to compute the regional totals, and the 2024 report reuses them unchanged (@va22_w); the sidebar split (50/24/6/4/11/5) is an alternative presentation.
remaining_uncertainty: No methodology note in either report explains how Exhibit 14 rows were weighted; BCG not contacted.

topic: South Korea share of 2019 semiconductor value added
disagreement: SIA/BCG's published 2019 Korea total is 16% (matching CSET's HQ-based 16%), but recomputing from SIA/BCG's own activity rows gives about 12.8%.
possible_reasons: published total may have been computed with unrounded or differently weighted rows
possible transcription error in Exhibit 14 rows (memory row shows Korea 59%)
row weights in Exhibit 14 may not be the weights used for the total
rationale: Neither can be preferred without BCG's underlying table; the 2022 exhibit reproduces cleanly (@va22_check), so the 2019 inconsistency appears specific to that exhibit.
remaining_uncertainty: Whether the 2019-2022 drop in Korea's total (16% to 12%) is real or partly an artefact.

topic: Wafer-size equivalence basis of SIA/BCG 2024 capacity figures
disagreement: SIA's summary labels the 1990-2032 capacity-share chart 'All values shown in 8” equivalents' while the full report's identical chart says '300 mm (12”) equivalents'.
possible_reasons: summary editing error
shares are invariant to the equivalence basis if conversion is by wafer area, so the label may have been treated as immaterial
rationale: The full report states the basis twice (Exhibit 7 note and the 1,121 kwspm '300 mm equivalents' sentence) and its absolute numbers convert consistently with SEMI totals (@equiv_inf).
remaining_uncertainty: Shares are unaffected; only absolute kwspm values depend on the basis.

topic: Vietnam share of global ATP capacity in 2032 (SIA/BCG 2024)
disagreement: SIA/BCG's text says Vietnam rises to 9% of global ATP capacity by 2032, but Exhibit 13's segment for Vietnam is labelled 8% (Malaysia is 9%).
possible_reasons: text may refer to a different rounding
label misplacement in the chart
text conflates Vietnam with Malaysia's 9%
rationale: Both appear in the same report; the chart is the more granular source, but the text is explicit.

topic: China's share of 2022 wafer capacity across publishers
disagreement: Mainland China's capacity share is 24% in SIA/BCG 2022 (8-inch+ fabs, 300mm-eq), 22% of 300mm capacity (SEMI 2022), 21% of 200mm capacity (SEMI 2022), 19.1% of IC capacity at end-2023 (Knometa) and 22% of all capacity in 2020 (CSET from SEMI).
possible_reasons: population: IC-only (Knometa) vs all semiconductors incl. discretes (SEMI/BCG)
wafer-size scope: 200mm only, 300mm only, or 8-inch-and-larger
fab thresholds (BCG excludes <5K wspm and R&D fabs)
year 2020 vs 2022 vs 2023
rationale: Figures measure different populations; the gap between Knometa (IC-only) and SIA/BCG (includes DAO, where China is 25%) is consistent with China's large discrete/power base (@oecd_pow).
remaining_uncertainty: No publisher gives China's share on all three bases for the same year.

disagreement: SIA/BCG forecast China's share peaking at 24% in 2025 and easing to 21-22% by 2030-2032, while SEMI's June 2024 release implies China at about 30% of 2025 capacity and Knometa expects China to become the largest region by 2026.
possible_reasons: SEMI counts all wafer sizes and small fabs (China has many <8-inch and small fabs)
BCG allocates future capex by announced projects to March 2024 and may underweight unannounced Chinese mature-node builds
OECD notes Chinese capacity is likely under-reported
rationale: Different populations and vintages; SEMI's figure is the more current measured base, BCG's the only long-range forecast.
remaining_uncertainty: Whether China's share will fall after 2025 as BCG projects.

topic: US share of leading-edge / advanced logic capacity by 2030-2032
disagreement: SIA/BCG project US 28% of <10nm logic capacity by 2032; Commerce projects at least 20% of leading-edge logic chips by 2030; TrendForce 17% of 16/14nm-and-below foundry capacity by 2027; OECD already shows the US with 0.84M of about 2.8M+ WSPM of <20nm capacity in 2025.
possible_reasons: node bin: <10nm vs 'leading edge' (Commerce, roughly 5nm and below) vs 16/14nm and below vs <20nm
population: all logic vs foundry only
capacity vs chips produced
target year 2027/2030/2032
rationale: Not comparable; each is internally consistent with its own definition.
remaining_uncertainty: Commerce's 'leading-edge' definition and method are not disclosed in the Vision document.

topic: Taiwan share of foundry vs all-logic capacity
disagreement: TrendForce puts Taiwan at about 46% of 2023 foundry capacity, while SIA/BCG put Taiwan at 30% of >=28nm logic and 40% of 10-22nm logic in 2022, and CSET (SEMI 2020) at 35% of all logic capacity.
possible_reasons: foundry-only population excludes IDM logic capacity (Intel, Texas Instruments, Infineon, etc.)
different years and node bins

topic: China's share of 2027 mature-node foundry capacity (TrendForce)
disagreement: Two TrendForce releases two months apart forecast China's 2027 mature-node foundry share at 33% (Oct 2023, >28nm) and 39% (Dec 2023, 28nm and older).
possible_reasons: definition: >28nm vs >=28nm (28nm itself is a large Chinese node)
model update between releases
